examples.ko: 회사가 은행에서 빌린 차입금을 천천히 갚고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is slowly paying back the loan it took from the bank.
I'm worried because the interest on the loan has gone up too much.
I paid back half of the loan this month.
If the debt is large, it becomes hard to run a company.

examples.ko: 집을 사려고 받은 차입금은 언제까지 갚아야 해요?
examples.en: By when do I have to repay the loan I took out to buy a house?

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 그 기업의 차입금이 크게 늘었다고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said that company's borrowings have grown a lot.

explain: '빌린 돈'은 일상 말이고, '차입금'은 회사·은행·뉴스에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 친구에게 빌린 돈에는 잘 안 써요. 반대로 빌려준 돈은 '대여금'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '빌린 돈' is the everyday phrase, while '차입금' is a formal word used for companies, banks and the news. You wouldn't normally use it for money borrowed from a friend. Money you lend out is called '대여금'.

examples.en: The company borrowed a large sum from the bank.
To build a factory, we have to borrow money.

examples.ko: 낮은 이자로 차입할 수 있는 방법이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a way to borrow at a low interest rate?

examples.ko: 그 나라는 해외에서 자금을 차입하고 있어요.
examples.en: That country is borrowing funds from abroad.
They borrowed in a hurry and paid the employees' salaries.
This time we decided not to borrow money.

explain: '빌리다'보다 훨씬 딱딱해서 회사나 나라가 은행, 외국에서 돈을 빌릴 때 주로 써요. 친구에게 돈을 빌릴 때는 그냥 '빌리다'라고 해요. 보통 '돈을/자금을 차입하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is much more formal than '빌리다' and is mainly used when a company or country borrows money from a bank or from abroad. For borrowing from a friend, just say '빌리다'. It usually appears with an object, like '돈을/자금을 차입하다'.

examples.ko: 이번 대회의 차점자는 우승자와 한 점 차이였어요.
examples.en: The runner-up in this contest was only one point behind the winner.
The runner-up can also receive a scholarship.
If the first-place person gives up, the runner-up moves up instead.
I narrowly failed the exam as the runner-up.

examples.ko: 선거에서 차점자와의 표 차이가 아주 작았어요.
examples.en: In the election, the vote gap with the runner-up was very small.
They gave a small prize to the runner-up as well.

explain: 보통 말로는 '2등'이라고 하고, '차점자'는 선거·시험·공모전 같은 공식 발표나 기사에서 써요. 꼭 2등이라는 순위보다 '아깝게 못 뽑힌 사람'이라는 느낌이 들 때가 많아요.
explain_en: In casual talk people say '2등', while '차점자' appears in official announcements and news about elections, exams and contests. It often carries a feel of 'the one who just missed being chosen'.

examples.en: Setting the result aside, I acknowledge your effort.
Let's put the cost issue aside for now.

examples.ko: 다른 건 다 차치하더라도 안전이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: Even if we set everything else aside, safety matters most.

examples.ko: 가격은 차치하고 디자인이 정말 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: Price aside, I really like the design.
Please set the minor mistakes aside and move on.

examples.ko: 그 문제를 차치하면 계획은 거의 완벽해요.
examples.en: If you leave that problem aside, the plan is nearly perfect.

explain: 거의 '~은/는 차치하고'의 꼴로 써요. 뒤에 오는 말이 더 중요하다는 느낌을 주고, 말보다는 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '~은 제쳐 두고', '~은 말고'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used almost always in the form '~은/는 차치하고', and it signals that what follows is more important. It appears more in writing and presentations than in talk. In casual speech people say '제쳐 두고' or '~은 말고'.

examples.ko: 직원이 회사 돈을 착복해서 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: An employee embezzled company money, and it became a problem.

examples.ko: 공금을 착복한 사람이 경찰 조사를 받아요.
examples.en: The person who embezzled public funds is being questioned by the police.
A rumor went around that the donations had been pocketed.
He altered the books in order to embezzle the money.

examples.ko: 남의 월급을 착복하면 절대 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must never keep someone else's wages for yourself.

examples.ko: 그 단체는 후원금을 착복하지 않았다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The organization said it did not misappropriate the sponsorship money.

explain: 맡은 돈이나 물건을 자기 것처럼 몰래 쓸 때 쓰고, 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보여요. 보통 '공금/기부금/월급을 착복하다'처럼 돈과 함께 써요. 일상에서는 '떼먹다', '가로채다'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone secretly keeps money or goods entrusted to them, and it shows up often in news. It usually pairs with money, as in '공금/기부금/월급을 착복하다'. In everyday talk people also say '떼먹다' or '가로채다'.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 색소로 착색해서 색이 진해요.
examples.en: This snack is colored with dye, so the color is deep.

examples.ko: 식품을 착색할 때는 안전한 재료를 써야 해요.
examples.en: When coloring food, you must use safe ingredients.
At the factory, they tint the glass blue.
If you color it with natural ingredients, the color is subtle.

examples.ko: 이 사탕은 인공 색소로 착색하지 않았어요.
examples.en: This candy is not colored with artificial dye.

examples.ko: 나무를 갈색으로 착색했더니 훨씬 고급스러워 보여요.
examples.en: After I stained the wood brown, it looks much more high-class.

explain: 식품, 유리, 나무처럼 원래 색이 없거나 다른 것에 색을 입힐 때 쓰고, 식품 성분 표시나 제품 설명에서 자주 보여요. 일상에서 그림을 칠할 때는 '색칠하다', '물들이다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when adding color to things like food, glass or wood, and it often appears in ingredient labels and product descriptions. For painting a picture in daily life, use '색칠하다' or '물들이다'.

examples.ko: 매일 착실히 공부하면 시험을 잘 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you study diligently every day, you can do well on the exam.

examples.ko: 그는 돈을 착실히 모아서 집을 샀어요.
examples.en: He saved money steadily and bought a house.

examples.ko: 착실히 준비한 만큼 결과가 좋을 거예요.
examples.en: The result will be as good as how steadily you prepared.

examples.ko: 저는 요즘 운동을 착실히 하고 있어요.
examples.en: These days I'm exercising faithfully.

examples.ko: 일을 착실히 해 온 직원이라 믿을 수 있어요.
examples.en: He's an employee who has worked reliably, so you can trust him.
Things are moving along steadily as planned.

explain: 서두르지 않고 성실하게 꾸준히 한다는 칭찬의 느낌이 있어요. '열심히'는 힘껏 한다는 느낌이고, '착실히'는 빠뜨리지 않고 차근차근 한다는 느낌이에요. 사람에게는 '착실하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It has a complimentary feel of doing something steadily and sincerely without rushing. '열심히' stresses effort, while '착실히' stresses doing things step by step without skipping. For a person, say '착실하다'.

examples.en: I have mixed feelings after hearing my friend's news.
With graduation coming up, my feelings are all mixed.
He looked out the window with a troubled expression.
I was both happy and sad, so my heart was in a tangle.

examples.ko: 이사하는 날 빈 집을 보니 착잡하더라고요.
examples.en: On moving day, seeing the empty house left me with mixed feelings.

examples.ko: 마음이 착잡해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: My feelings were so tangled that I couldn't say anything.

explain: 기쁨과 슬픔, 걱정이 한꺼번에 섞여 마음이 복잡하고 무거울 때 써요. '복잡하다'보다 감정이 무겁고 쓸쓸한 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '마음이/기분이 착잡하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it when joy, sadness and worry are mixed together and your heart feels heavy and tangled. Compared with '복잡하다', it carries a stronger sense of heaviness and loneliness. It is usually used as '마음이/기분이 착잡하다'.

examples.ko: 팀원들이 일을 착착 나눠서 금방 끝났어요.
examples.en: The team members split up the work smoothly, so it finished quickly.
The soldiers walk along with their steps in neat unison.
The preparations are moving along smoothly.
He sorts the documents neatly, one after another.

examples.ko: 모든 일이 계획대로 착착 되어 가요.
examples.en: Everything is going according to plan without a hitch.

examples.ko: 젖은 옷이 몸에 착착 달라붙어서 불편해요.
examples.en: The wet clothes cling to my body, and it's uncomfortable.

explain: 일이 막힘없이 순서대로 잘 되어 갈 때 가장 많이 써요. 젖은 것이 달라붙는 모습에도 쓰는데, 이때는 '착착 달라붙다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '척척'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is most often used when things go ahead smoothly and in order without any holdups. It also describes wet things clinging to something, as in '착착 달라붙다'. A similar word is '척척'.

examples.en: The students sang a hymn in praise of spring.
This song is a hymn to love.

examples.ko: 시인은 자연의 찬가라고 할 만한 시를 썼어요.
examples.en: The poet wrote a poem you could call a hymn to nature.

examples.ko: 졸업식에서 학교 찬가를 다 함께 불렀어요.
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony, we all sang the school anthem together.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 청춘에 바치는 찬가 같아요.
examples.en: That movie feels like an ode to youth.
A victory anthem rang out across the stadium.

explain: 누군가를 칭찬하고 기리는 노래나 글이라서, 실제 노래뿐 아니라 '청춘의 찬가'처럼 작품의 분위기를 말할 때도 써요. 나라를 대표하는 노래는 '국가'라고 하고, '찬가'와 구별해요.
explain_en: It is a song or writing that praises and honors something, so besides actual songs you can say things like '청춘의 찬가' for the mood of a work. A national anthem is '국가', which is different from '찬가'.

examples.en: On my way home from work, I bought side-dish ingredients at the market.
I have nothing to make side dishes with for tonight.
Do you want to go to the mart with me to buy groceries for side dishes?
Grandmother picked some vegetables for side dishes from her garden.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 찬거리가 떨어져서 장을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: We've run out of food in the fridge, so I need to go shopping.

examples.ko: 찬거리 걱정 때문에 매일 메뉴를 고민해요.
examples.en: I worry about what to cook every day because of the side-dish ingredients.

explain: 밥과 함께 먹을 반찬을 만들 재료를 말해요. 장 본 것 전체가 아니라 반찬 재료만 가리켜요. '반찬거리'라고도 해요. 주로 집에서 요리하는 상황에서 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the ingredients for side dishes to eat with rice, not to everything you bought while shopping. People also say '반찬거리'. It is mainly used when talking about cooking at home.

examples.en: I fully support the team leader's opinion.
Many people agreed with the new rule.
Not everyone supported that plan.
At the meeting, there was nobody who agreed.

examples.ko: 친구의 생각에 찬동하고 싶지만 걱정이 돼요.
examples.en: I'd like to side with my friend's idea, but I'm worried.
My parents also approved of my decision.

explain: '찬성하다'와 비슷하지만 의견이나 생각에 마음으로 같이한다는 느낌이 더 있어요. 주로 '~에 찬동하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 써요. 말보다는 글이나 공식적인 자리에서 더 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It is close to '찬성하다' but leans more toward agreeing with an opinion or idea in spirit. It is usually used with the particle '에', as in '~에 찬동하다'. It appears more in writing and formal settings than in casual speech.

examples.ko: 아침 해가 바다 위로 찬란히 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: The morning sun rose radiantly over the sea.
The stars shine brilliantly in the night sky.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 오래전에 찬란히 꽃핀 문화를 가졌어요.
examples.en: This city had a culture that bloomed magnificently long ago.
The chandelier sparkled brilliantly from the ceiling.
His name remained in history with glory.

examples.ko: 졸업하는 날 아침 해가 찬란히 빛났어요.
examples.en: On graduation day, the morning sun shone brilliantly.

explain: 눈부시게 빛나는 모습이나, 훌륭하고 화려한 역사·문화를 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서 가볍게 쓰기보다 글이나 감동적인 장면에서 많이 보여요. 형용사는 '찬란하다'예요.
explain_en: It describes something shining dazzlingly, or a splendid history or culture. It appears more in writing and moving scenes than in light everyday talk. The adjective form is '찬란하다'.

examples.en: The debate over the new law is heated.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 공사에 대해 찬반양론이 나뉘었어요.
examples.en: Opinions split into for and against over the construction in front of the school.
The arguments for and against were so evenly matched that we couldn't decide.
The news covered the pros and cons of the school uniform issue.

examples.ko: 이 주제는 늘 찬반양론이 있는 이야기예요.
examples.en: This topic always has people arguing on both sides.
In the debate, I listened to both sides of the argument.

explain: 찬성하는 의견과 반대하는 의견이 둘 다 있다는 뜻으로 뉴스나 토론에서 많이 써요. '찬반양론이 팽팽하다', '찬반양론이 나뉘다'처럼 자주 말해요. 줄여서 '찬반'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is common in news and debates to say that opinions both for and against exist. You often hear '찬반양론이 팽팽하다' or '찬반양론이 나뉘다'. It is also shortened to '찬반'.

examples.en: The alumni association collected donations and held an event.

examples.ko: 회사가 우리 축제에 찬조금을 내 주었어요.
examples.en: The company gave a contribution to our festival.

examples.ko: 찬조금을 낸 분들의 이름이 벽에 붙었어요.
examples.en: The names of the people who gave donations were put up on the wall.

examples.ko: 졸업 파티를 위해 선배들이 찬조금을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The seniors sent money to help with the graduation party.
A lot of donations came in, so the event was rich.
Even a small contribution is a big help.

explain: '기부금'은 널리 돕는 돈이고, '찬조금'은 학교 행사, 동창회, 대회처럼 특정 모임이나 행사를 도우려고 내는 돈이라는 느낌이에요. 보통 '찬조금을 내다/받다'로 써요.
explain_en: '기부금' is money given as general charity, while '찬조금' feels like money given to help a particular gathering or event, such as a school event, alumni meeting or contest. It is usually used as '찬조금을 내다/받다'.

examples.en: The owner kindly sponsored prizes for the event.
Local shops sponsored the contest.

examples.ko: 동문 한 분이 장학금을 찬조하기로 했어요.
examples.en: One alumnus decided to contribute a scholarship.
If a company sponsors an event, it also works as advertising.
I'm grateful to the person who donated the gifts.

examples.ko: 이번 축제는 여러 기업이 찬조해서 열렸어요.
examples.en: This festival was held with sponsorship from several companies.

explain: 행사나 모임을 돕기 위해 돈이나 물건을 내놓을 때 써요. '후원하다'와 비슷하지만 일회성 행사를 돕는 느낌이 더 강해요. '상품을 찬조하다'처럼 물건에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when giving money or goods to help an event or gathering. It is similar to '후원하다' but feels more like helping a one-off event. It also works with goods, as in '상품을 찬조하다'.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 성격이 찬찬해서 실수가 적어요.
examples.en: That child has a calm, careful personality, so he or she makes few mistakes.
He's a careful person, so I feel safe entrusting him with work.

examples.ko: 찬찬하게 설명해 주셔서 이해가 잘 됐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to your calm, careful explanation, I understood well.
The teacher's way of speaking is always calm and unhurried.
He handles his work carefully and steadily.

examples.ko: 동생은 찬찬하지 않고 늘 급하게 움직여요.
examples.en: My younger sibling isn't careful and always moves in a hurry.

explain: 실제로는 '찬찬히'의 꼴로 가장 많이 써요. 서두르지 않고 꼼꼼하고 차분하게 한다는 느낌이에요. '천천히'는 속도가 느린 것이고, '찬찬히'는 꼼꼼하고 침착하게 한다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: In practice it appears most often as '찬찬히'. It has a feel of being unhurried, thorough and calm. '천천히' is about slow speed, while '찬찬히' stresses doing it carefully and composedly.

examples.en: The audience marveled at the wonderful performance.
Everyone marvels at his singing ability.

examples.ko: 이렇게 아름다운 풍경에는 찬탄하지 않을 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't help but marvel at such a beautiful view.
The teacher also marveled at the student's painting.

examples.ko: 손님들이 한복을 보고 찬탄하며 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The guests took photos, admiring the hanbok.
It was such great skill that it was worth marveling at.

explain: '칭찬하다'가 말로 좋게 평가하는 것이라면, '찬탄하다'는 너무 훌륭해서 저절로 감탄이 나오는 느낌이에요. 보통 '~에 찬탄하다'로 쓰고, 일상 대화보다 글에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: While '칭찬하다' means to give praise in words, '찬탄하다' feels like admiration bursting out because something is so wonderful. It is usually used as '~에 찬탄하다' and appears more in writing than in daily conversation.

examples.en: I filled the cup with water right up to the brim.

examples.ko: 호수의 물이 찰랑찰랑 가장자리까지 차 있어요.
examples.en: The lake water is filled right up to the edge.

examples.ko: 국을 너무 가득 담아서 찰랑찰랑 넘칠 것 같아요.
examples.en: I filled the soup so full that it looks about to spill over.
Her hair swayed lightly in the wind.

examples.ko: 잔이 찰랑 차오를 때까지 따라 주세요.
examples.en: Please pour until the glass is filled to the brim.
It rained, so the rice paddy is brimming with water.

explain: 물이 가득 차서 가장자리에서 살짝 흔들리는 모습에 써요. 보통 '찰랑찰랑'처럼 두 번 반복해서 말해요. 가벼운 머리카락이나 장신구가 흔들리는 모습에도 써요.
explain_en: It describes liquid filled right to the edge and gently rippling there. People usually repeat it as '찰랑찰랑'. It can also describe light hair or accessories swaying.

examples.en: When the wind blows, her hair sways lightly.
The water in the bowl was about to slosh, so I carried it carefully.
The waves lapped gently at my ankles.
The way her earrings dangle and sway is pretty.
I poured juice until the glass was almost overflowing.
Her skirt sways lightly with every step.

explain: 물이 가득 차서 흔들리거나, 가벼운 머리카락·치맛자락이 부드럽게 흔들릴 때 써요. '출렁거리다'는 물결이 더 크게 흔들리는 느낌이라 구별해서 써요. 줄여서 '찰랑이다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for a full container of water gently sloshing, or for light hair or skirts swaying softly. '출렁거리다' feels like bigger, heavier movement, so the two are used differently. It can also be shortened to '찰랑이다'.

examples.en: A wave slapped against the rock.
The child clung tightly to his mother's back.
I slapped my arm to catch a mosquito.
The fish slapped the water with its tail.
The wet clothes stuck right to my body.
My friend gave my shoulder a slap and laughed.

explain: 물이나 손바닥이 납작하게 닿을 때 나는 소리와, 딱 달라붙는 모습을 모두 나타내요. '철썩'은 소리가 더 크고 센 느낌이고, '찰싹'은 더 가볍고 작은 느낌이에요. 소리가 반복될 때는 '찰싹찰싹'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It expresses both the sound of water or a palm hitting flatly and the look of something sticking tightly. '철썩' sounds bigger and heavier, while '찰싹' feels lighter and smaller. For repeated sounds, say '찰싹찰싹'.
